summary: 28Mn5Ni is the Ni-bearing austenitic low-density steel (LDS) grade Fe-28Mn-9Al-5Ni-0.9C produced by vacuum induction melting, homogenisation at 1423 K for 2 h and hot rolling at 1323 K (~85% total thickness reduction). It is the B2-containing counterpart of the B2-free 28Mn0Ni grade: its hot-rolled microstructure consists of a γ (austenite) matrix with fine κ-carbides plus ~4% intergranular B2 ordered Fe(Ni)Al particles (~300 nm) associated with DO3 ordered Fe3Al, and the highest annealing-twin fraction (~40%) of the three alloys studied. The paper asks how alloy chemistry (Mn, Ni) and the resulting B2 phase control the deformation behaviour of hot-rolled LDS, using this alloy as the intermediate-B2-fraction case between B2-free 28Mn0Ni and B2-stringer-rich 15Mn5Ni.
composition: Nominal composition Fe-28Mn-9Al-5Ni-0.9C (wt%); deliberately designed as the Ni-containing grade with high Mn, at nearly constant Al and C levels (Table 1). The analysed chemistry of the homogenised ingot is Mn 28.1 wt%, Al 8.6 wt%, C 0.9 wt%, Ni 4.8 wt%, Fe balance. Mn and Ni contents were chosen on the basis of austenite stability to produce a B2-containing (rather than B2-free) γ-matrix; Ni is added specifically to promote the ordered Fe(Ni)Al B2 phase, which is known to raise the strength of LDS. Solute partitioning is pronounced: the γ matrix of the hot-rolled alloy is Fe-27.8Mn-7.5Al-5.7Ni (wt%), whereas the B2 phase is much richer in Al and Ni and poorer in Mn: Fe-16.3Mn-13.6Al-21.5Ni (wt%). Both SEM-EDS and TEM-EDS confirm this clear partitioning between γ and B2 with no compositional gradient within individual B2 grains.
